title: Concept: Spring Security permits every request in java — review required
description: In java, the authorization chain ends with anyRequest().permitAll(). Spring then treats every request as allowed once it reaches the filter, so a controller added months later is exposed by default rather than protected by default. Authentication may still run, but no authorization decision is made, and nothing in the configuration records which endpoints were meant to be public.
applicability: java services using Spring Security HttpSecurity configuration.
risk: Unauthenticated access to every mapped endpoint; HIGH severity.
